wa_e_near_end_aka_twin_cracks_area.blurb: The first wall most visitors reach on the Sunshine Wall at Vantage (Frenchman Coulee), central Washington. It is mostly a trad crag, with a handful of bolted lines and a single boulder problem, and the routes run from moderate up to the low 5.11 range, with a good number in the 5.8 to 5.10 band. Expect sunny, warm desert climbing that suits late fall through early spring; summer can be brutal, so carry plenty of water. The wall is often busy. You get to it by walking through a narrow corridor on the trail, and the cliff is just beyond the bend. Watch for drop-offs near the base if you bring children or dogs.

wa_north_side_the.blurb: One of the main sections of The Feathers at Vantage (Frenchman Coulee), a beginner-friendly cluster of free-standing eroded basalt columns. Nearly all of the climbing here is bolted, with a few trad lines and one top-rope. Grades start at 5.0-ish beginner terrain and top out around 5.10, with most routes sitting between 5.7 and 5.10, so it works well for people new to leading outdoors. The north-facing side stays shaded, which makes it a sensible hot-weather choice. The car is only a few steps from the base on flat ground. The Feathers get very crowded, and many first bolts are set high, so a stick-clip is handy.

wa_nevermind_wall.blurb: A hard-leaning sport wall at Exit 38 (Deception Crags) near North Bend, about half an hour from Seattle. The rock is the area's blocky, juggy metamorphic stone. Our catalog holds mostly sport routes plus a couple of boulder problems, and almost everything is 5.10 or harder, running up into the 5.12s; there is next to nothing below 5.9. Ledges are scarce, so belay spots are cramped, and the wall sees light traffic because of the difficulty. Lines often need a brush in spring and early summer, and some seep after rain. Reach it by crossing the railroad trestle on the Iron Horse Trail, then a short steep trail on the right.
wa_nevermind_wall.parking_note: From I-90 take Exit 38 and follow the signs toward Olallie State Park. Roughly a half mile along the road you will find gravel pullouts on the left, just before the creek crossing. Don't leave valuables in the car; break-ins have been reported here.
wa_nevermind_wall.approach: Hike uphill from the pullouts to the railroad grade (Iron Horse Trail), cross the bridge over the creek gorge, then turn right and scramble up a short, steep trail with a hand-line to the base of the wall.

wa_woods_the.blurb: A group of crags at Exit 32 (Little Si) outside North Bend, tucked in the last cluster west of the Mt Si trail. Nearly everything here is bolted, with a few trad lines and a top-rope. The rock is the volcanic metamorphic stone typical of the North Bend area, mostly clean and free of loose choss. It leans hard: from our catalog, most routes fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with only a couple below that, making it a good stop for those climbing in the 5.11 to 5.12 range. Trailhead parking is very limited and fills early. Climbing is restricted to designated areas, and new route development is not permitted outside existing ones.
